blueprint.title: Repair Ledger Replay Pipeline and SQL Ingestion Filter
blueprint.scenario: A financial analytics database replica relies on an ordered ingestion pipeline where raw daily SQL transaction streams pass through a compiled C validator (`/usr/local/bin/sqlsieve`) before being applied sequentially to SQLite partition databases and rolled into `/var/lib/analytics/reporting.db`. Following an upstream SQL dialect update, the validator misclassifies legitimate statements containing multi-line block comments and escaped string literals while allowing malformed schema injections through, causing the multi-stage shell replay runner (`/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh`) to halt midway and leave the database in an inconsistent, partially migrated state.
blueprint.instruction_draft: Hey, our reporting numbers stopped adding up after last week's upstream dialect changes. It looks like `sqlsieve` is misfiltering transactions—dropping valid adjustment batches and letting bad inputs slip past—and `replay_ledger.sh` dies halfway through, leaving the replica corrupted. Could you get `sqlsieve` patched and rebuilt, fix the replay script so it recovers from errors and processes the backlog partition stages in the right order, and rebuild `/var/lib/analytics/reporting.db`? Malicious and malformed statements need to be quarantined in `/var/log/quarantine.log`, all legitimate entries must be reflected in the ledger, and the `ledger_summary` table has to match.
requirements: Patch the C source code in `/opt/sqlsieve/src/` and recompile `/usr/local/bin/sqlsieve` so that it accurately validates SQL ledger transaction statements.

Ensure `sqlsieve` correctly accepts all valid SQL statements—including multi-line comments (`/* ... */`), escaped quote literals (`''` and `\'`), and savepoint transactions—while rejecting malformed SQL syntax, unescaped quote injections, and prohibited DDL operations (e.g., unauthorized `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, or `ATTACH DATABASE`).

Update `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh` to implement proper error recovery: non-zero validator rejections must divert rejected lines into `/var/log/quarantine.log` with a timestamp and statement hash without aborting the batch replay.

Ensure `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh` executes the migration and transaction replay in strict partition dependency order (partition snapshot -> sequential daily journals -> aggregate rollup), rolling back partial transaction chunks if a runtime SQLite failure occurs within a single valid batch.
Re-run the full ledger replay pipeline so that `/var/lib/analytics/reporting.db` is completely rebuilt and consistent, populated with all valid records and an updated `ledger_summary` table.
environment: Dockerfile installs `gcc`, `make`, `sqlite3`, `libsqlite3-dev`, `python3`, and standard shell utilities (`bash`, `coreutils`, `gawk`, `sed`).

Source code for the SQL pre-filtering engine located at `/opt/sqlsieve/` with `Makefile` and `src/validator.c` (~950 lines of C implementing a lexer/parser state machine for transaction SQL statements).
Compiled binary `/usr/local/bin/sqlsieve` pre-built during Docker build.

Shell orchestration script `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh` (~300 lines) which orchestrates unpacking compressed partition archives from `/var/backlog/`, calling `sqlsieve`, feeding valid statements into `sqlite3 /var/lib/analytics/reporting.db`, and generating summary tables.
Seed partition backlog in `/var/backlog/partition_*.sql.gz` containing hundreds of historical ledger entries with a mix of valid records, edge-case syntax, and corrupted injection statements.

Plant in C code: the tokenizer state machine resets state prematurely upon seeing `*` inside comments and fails to handle backslash escapes inside single quotes, causing false-positive rejections on valid rows and false-negative passes on split-payload comments.

Plant in shell script: lacks transaction isolation around individual batch imports, crashes on the first non-zero exit from `sqlsieve` instead of redirecting to quarantine, and processes partition files using unsorted glob expansion (`partition_*.sql.gz`) which breaks sequential foreign key and balance dependencies.
blueprint.internal_hint: Inspect `/opt/sqlsieve/src/validator.c` to locate state machine defects: (1) multi-line comment state transition in `scan_token()` terminates on any standalone `*` rather than `*/`, causing multiline comments with asterisks to be treated as malformed SQL; (2) string escape parser only checks for SQL-standard `''` doubling but ignores POSIX/C-style `\'` escapes emitted by the new upstream service, causing single quotes to terminate string literals prematurely and trigger syntax errors on legitimate notes; (3) blocklist inspection fails to check token boundaries for `ATTACH` and `DROP` if preceded by trailing whitespace or semicolons within a multi-statement block. After fixing the C source, recompile via `make -C /opt/sqlsieve install`. Then inspect `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh`: change glob order to `sort -V` across partitions so snapshots are loaded before daily increments, wrap each day's replay in an explicit `BEGIN TRANSACTION ... COMMIT` block with rollback on failure, and redirect validator stderr/rejected statements into `/var/log/quarantine.log` so legitimate records continue processing. Finally, execute `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh` to rebuild `/var/lib/analytics/reporting.db`.
blueprint.trap: A solver might only test against the visible sample in `/var/backlog/` by patching the shell script to ignore `sqlsieve` exit codes or simply grepping for keyword `DROP`, which allows malicious statements to execute or drops complex multi-line comment adjustments; or the solver sorts partition files lexically (`partition_10.sql` before `partition_2.sql`) instead of natural version order (`sort -V`), silently corrupting cumulative balances in `ledger_summary`.
tests: Verify `sqlsieve` binary exists and matches the newly compiled target from `/opt/sqlsieve`.

Execute `sqlsieve` against an adversarial corpus of 200 hidden statements generated at verify time from a hidden seed (100 benign statements with edge-case comments, nested quotes, escaped characters, and valid DDL/DML; 100 malicious/malformed statements containing unauthorized `ATTACH`, `DROP TABLE`, unclosed quotes, and stacked injections), verifying 100% precision and recall.
Verify `/var/log/quarantine.log` exists, is non-empty, and correctly records all rejected statements with required hash and timestamp metadata.
Execute an end-to-end replay test using a fresh, hidden partition set generated at test time, verifying that `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh` completes cleanly with exit code 0.

Query `/var/lib/analytics/reporting.db` using SQLite to check schema integrity (`PRAGMA integrity_check`), foreign key consistency (`PRAGMA foreign_key_check`), and compare computed balances in `ledger_summary` against the ground-truth reference values.

verifier_knob.name: adversarial_corpus_density
verifier_knob.value: 200 synthetic statements (100 benign edge-cases, 100 adversarial/corrupt variants)
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing the count and syntactic diversity (e.g., unicode escapes, mixed line endings, nested comments) demands strict conformance in the C lexer, while decreasing it allows looser regex-based parsing to slip through.

expected_failure_modes: Agent edits `/usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh` to pipe raw SQL directly into SQLite without fixing the C binary, causing malicious injections or broken statements to corrupt the database.
Agent patches `validator.c` for standard SQL `''` escapes but forgets backslash escaping `\'`, failing the hidden corpus evaluation.

Agent fails to enforce ordered partition processing (`sort -V`), causing transaction snapshots to be evaluated after incremental updates, which produces negative account balances and foreign-key violations.
Agent fails to implement error quarantine in the shell script, causing the script to either crash on the first invalid entry or silently drop the rest of the batch.

speedrun: sed -i 's/case \*:/case \*\/:/' /opt/sqlsieve/src/validator.c # or manual edit of comment transition
patch /opt/sqlsieve/src/validator.c <<'EOF' # add backslash escape handling in string scanner and fix token delimiter check for forbidden keywords EOF
patch /usr/local/bin/replay_ledger.sh <<'EOF' # sort partitions via sort -V, route sqlsieve non-zero to /var/log/quarantine.log with sha256/timestamp, wrap batch in BEGIN/COMMIT EOF
invalid_failure_risks: Quarantine log format mismatch: The requirements and tests check for 'required hash and timestamp metadata', but the instruction only vaguely asks for statements to be quarantined in '/var/log/quarantine.log' without specifying hash algorithm (SHA256 vs MD5), timestamp format (ISO-8601 vs Unix epoch), or delimiter/field order.

Hidden corpus edge cases: Demanding 100% precision and recall on 200 hidden synthetic SQL statements against a hand-written ~950-line C tokenizer will cause false test failures on standard SQLite syntax quirks not covered by the existing codebase.
Prohibited statement scope: The instruction mentions 'malicious and malformed statements', but doesn't specify the exact set of forbidden DDL/DML rules (e.g., DROP, ATTACH, TRUNCATE).
review.reasons: The user instruction omits critical requirements that the evaluation tests enforce, particularly the exact schema, hashing algorithm, and timestamp format for `/var/log/quarantine.log`. Furthermore, evaluating a custom C SQL tokenizer against 200 hidden adversarial/benign statements with a 100% precision/recall requirement without a precise dialect grammar specification creates high risk of invalid failures due to dialect nuances.
fixes: Specify the exact quarantine log entry format in the instruction (or pre-define a `log_quarantine` function in `replay_ledger.sh`), e.g., `<ISO8601_TIMESTAMP> <SHA256_HEX> <RAW_STATEMENT>`.

Provide an explicit rule specification or header file in `/opt/sqlsieve/include/rules.h` defining exactly what statements are forbidden (e.g., `ATTACH`, `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`) rather than leaving it to broad intuition.
Scope the hidden corpus tests to the documented subset of SQLite ledger statements supported by the C validator rather than open-ended general SQL syntax.
